motion: Is intelligent design a legitimate scientific explanation for biological origins?

bridges.description: Infer intelligent causation from biological information.
Use historical reasoning from effects to known causes.
Show design generates research and predictions.
Deny that origins warrant intelligent design.
Prefer coherent natural laws and evolution.
Continue inquiry rather than end with agency.

sections.title: Information and origins
sections.rationale: Whether functional biological information requires intelligence.

sections.title: Scientific method
sections.rationale: Whether historical causal inference may include intelligence.

sections.title: Evolutionary scope
sections.rationale: Origins, mutation, and later evolution remain distinct.

sections.title: Inquiry and closings
sections.rationale: Competing final views of scientific progress.

coverageAudit.omittedMaterialRationale: All retained blocks and both closings were reviewed. Omitted for capacity but not reversed: Meyer's order-information detail, Sternberg correction, Rosetta analogy, origins-context distinction, biblical-deduction distinction, acceptance of evolutionary biology as empirical, willingness to accept a demonstrated origin account, and noncoding-DNA example; Atkins's material-mind, interconnected-science, procedural-status, simple-process, and noncoding-priority replies. Repetition and tone-only exchanges are omitted. Haville and Brierley are context only. Film clips, promotions, feedback, and outro create no credit, penalty, concession, or reply obligation.
